routes.how_it_works: A Chift client becomes a Horus company (a customer or supplier record inside a folder) flagged as customer, created with companies.new. Creation returns only an id, so the connector reads back the company, its IBANs and its receivable account to build the response.
routes.documented: companies.new needs folder, search key, name, role and VAT-liable flags, language and country; it takes VAT number, one address, contacts, IBANs and receivable account, and returns only the id. A duplicate VAT number is refused by default; companies.update is partial.
depends_on_assumption: Proposal (C8): search key generated from the name, numeric suffix on collision (Horus rules undocumented); missing language and country taken from folder defaults.
Undocumented field use: active=false as CustomerActivitySuspended; a non-VAT-liable client's company_number as VatNumber; phone and website read back from ContactPhone and ContactWebsite.
Proposal: duplicates are caught by a pre-check on VAT number and external reference, since Horus documents no idempotency key.
needs_confirmation: Horus: search-key rules and duplicate-key error (H7, H6); meaning of CustomerActivitySuspended, how an enterprise number is written, default receivable account (H11).
Horus: is the duplicate-VAT check per folder, and does it ignore spaces and dots (H25)?
Chift: search-key convention, duplicate behaviour, force_merge policy, and whether unstorable fields or extra addresses are rejected or dropped (C8, C6, C3).
not_concluded: Whether a timed-out create can still be committed later; until known, the check before a retry is best effort (H3).
Whether companies.list can include IBANs and the receivable account in one call, shortening the read-back (H15).
routes.feasibility_reason: Creation, read-back and merge are documented; the search-key format, a few field meanings and the duplicate policy rest on assumptions or Chift decisions, none blocking.

considerations.text: A Horus 'company' is a customer or supplier inside a folder, not the Chift company or folder. One record can hold both roles, hence force_merge.
Horus requires a search key (the third-party code accountants see) that Chift does not send; the connector must generate one per folder. Proposal: derive it from the name (C8).

A VAT number already used by another company is refused by default (AllowDuplicateVatNumber=false), so a client that already exists as a supplier should go through force_merge rather than a duplicate company.
No idempotency key and no company delete endpoint: a blind retry can leave an undeletable duplicate, so the connector searches before retrying.

not_mappable: One address per company: extra invoice or delivery addresses are lost.
mobile, internal_notes, first_name, last_name, function, company_id: no field; dropped and returned null. Currency is read-only.
is_company=false: no company/individual flag, so every client comes back as a company.
Enterprise number of a VAT-liable client, and non-IBAN bank accounts, cannot be stored.

horus_main: POST /account-histories.list (+1 call for payments when requested)
routes.how_it_works: No Horus endpoint lists all invoices, so each is rebuilt from the ledger: headers from book-entries.list (one call per sales or purchase journal) and lines, VAT, analytics and matching from account-histories.list. For sales, the open sales invoices list adds payment status and invoice-currency amounts.
routes.documented: Pushed invoices become book entries in their daybook. book-entries.list gives headers per daybook and month period, account-histories.list gives lines with VAT, analytics and matching (both accept ModifiedAfter); the open sales list adds open amount, payment status, invoice currency.
depends_on_assumption: Proposal (H2, C2): invoice or credit note is decided by journal type; tax_code is rebuilt from line VAT fields, null when ambiguous.
Proposal (H4, C16): ledger amounts are EUR, so foreign-currency invoices return in EUR unless the open sales list gives the invoice currency.
Lists return full results (no paging documented); 'paid' is inferred from full matching; reference and memo are split from the header comment (H9).
needs_confirmation: Horus: can the document type be read, and can credit notes sit in invoice journals (H2)? Currency of ledger amounts and CurrencyRate direction (H4)?
Horus: limits on result size, period and request rate (H5); does ModifiedAfter catch payments and accountant edits (H10)?
Chift: default period, draft handling and re-sync cadence (C10, C11); acceptable misclassification (C5); invoice currency or stable EUR view (C16).
not_concluded: Performance on large folders: Horus documents no limits and no request was sent; to be measured on a test folder.
How deleted or replaced invoices are detected: no deletion signal is documented; webhooks are mentioned but not documented.
Whether the open sales invoices list ever returns fully paid invoices.
routes.feasibility_reason: Core invoice data is readable, but the invoice/credit-note split, foreign-currency amounts and large-folder behaviour depend on Horus answers (H2, H4, H5).

considerations.text: Query parameters shape the calls: date_from/date_to become the month window Horus requires (StartMonth/EndMonth) and are re-filtered to the day; journal_ids choose the daybooks read, one header call each; include_payments adds one ledger call; include_partner_info adds none, because book-entries.list can return the partners in the same response (Include = CompanyDetail.Company). The ledger-line call is made even when include_invoice_lines=false: payment status, due dates and currency come from the partner line.
Updating an invoice creates a new book entry with a new id, so stored ids stop working; reconcile on journal plus number.

Paging, day-level dates, payment_status and approval_status have no Horus parameter and are emulated; updated_after still reads a month window and misses deletions, so periodic full re-sync is needed.
There is no purchase-side open-invoice list, so purchase payment status comes only from matching on the ledger.

not_mappable: Line quantity, unit price and unit: not stored; lines return quantity 1 and unit price equal to the line amount.
delivery_date, payment_term_id, payment_method_id, withholding_tax and partner first and last names: no field on read; returned null.
No 'cancelled' status or approval workflow: approval_status stays 'unknown' unless Chift accepts Horus 'Verified' (C18).
Purchase VAT kind is not returned, so some tax_codes are null. Ledger lines carry a currency code and rate, but whether their amounts are in EUR or in that currency is undocumented (H4).

routes.how_it_works: Customer invoices and refunds go to invoices.sales.new, supplier ones to invoices.purchases.new (Type 0 invoice, 1 credit note), PDF included. The connector first resolves journal, partner, accounts, VAT combination and analytic codes, converts analytic percentages to amounts, checks the number, then reads the entry back.
routes.documented: Both endpoints take header totals, lines with VAT fields and analytics, currency, comment and an optional file. Horus checks that totals add up and accepts only its published tax combinations. Entries are unconfirmed by default; create returns only the id.
depends_on_assumption: Proposal (C2): each Chift tax_code is a connector-owned id for one accepted Horus VAT combination; VAT amounts are booked as sent.
Proposal (C1, H2): posting mode per connection, review (unconfirmed, default) or direct; credit notes sent as Type 1 with positive amounts.
Proposal (C9, C8): analytic percentages per plan become amounts on combined cost lines; partner_info.account_number is read as the third-party code.
needs_confirmation: Horus: are the tax-combination files current and complete, how are invalid combinations rejected (H1)? A test folder, since invoices cannot be deleted (H17).
Horus: numbering, number uniqueness and timed-out creates (H3); credit notes in invoice journals, negative amounts (H2); currency (H4); may every user confirm (H21)?
Chift: posting mode and meaning of 'draft' (C1); rule for unnumbered invoices (C7); reject or drop unstorable inputs (C3); meaning of partner_info.account_number (C8).
not_concluded: Effect of a mandatory free-typed analytic dimension or a locked cost section on posting (H13).
routes.feasibility_reason: The native endpoints cover the route, but the VAT catalogue (H1), numbering and duplicates (H3, C7) and posting status (C1) need answers first.

considerations.text: VAT is the main risk: Horus accepts no VAT code; each line needs rate, origin and type (plus kind and condition for purchases) from an accepted combination.
Numbers must be numeric and the API does not number invoices automatically; a number such as INV-2024/001 belongs in reference, not invoice_number.
API entries are unconfirmed by default, while Chift defaults to 'posted'; the response must report the status actually stored.
No endpoint deletes an invoice, so a wrong or duplicate one needs the accountant; hence a best-effort duplicate-number check before creating and before any retry.

not_mappable: withholding_tax and nl_payment_terms_split: no Horus field (Belgian and Luxembourg folders only). Proposal: reject with 422 (C3).
start_date, end_date, delivery_date, force_financial_period, payment_term_id: no field; the period follows the invoice date (Proposal: reject or log, C3).
Line quantity, unit price and unit are not stored; reference shares the header comment with customer_memo and cannot be filtered.
Automatic numbering unavailable (Proposal: unnumbered invoices go to review as draft, C7); currencies outside Horus's list are rejected.

routes.how_it_works: One Horus call lists every daybook (journal) of the folder with code, name, type, IBAN and currency. The connector maps the daybook type to the Chift journal type and looks up the counterpart account number in the cached chart of accounts.
routes.documented: daybooks.list returns per daybook its id, code, name, type, IBAN, currency settings and a reference to its counterpart account. The guide links types 100/150, 200/250, 500, 590 and 600 to posting endpoints; mapping them to Chift types is a deduction.
depends_on_assumption: Cash, temporary, system and cost daybooks (550, 610, 690, 700) are returned as blocked, as no API posting endpoint is documented for them.
Sales and purchase journals are assumed to accept other currencies (setting not exposed); an empty journal currency is read as the folder currency.
Proposal: next_document_numbers stays empty by default; an estimate from the highest existing number is opt-in, as numbering is undocumented.
needs_confirmation: Horus: can cash or temporary daybooks receive API entries, and what does IsUsed mean (H14)?
Horus: numbering format per daybook and fiscal year (H3), only if next document numbers are required.
Chift: is an empty next_document_numbers acceptable (C4), and should non-postable journals be listed as blocked or hidden?
not_concluded: Whether a daybook can be deactivated in Horus Office (the Horus accounting application): daybooks carry no status field and IsUsed is undocumented.
routes.feasibility_reason: Core journal fields come natively from one call; blocked, other_currencies_allowed and the type of less common daybooks rest on assumptions until Horus answers H14.

considerations.text: The daybook type decides which endpoint can post into a journal, so it is the routing key for every write route, not only this list.
journal_type describes the daybook, not each entry: Horus invoices carry their own invoice or credit-note type, so credit notes may sit in sales or purchase journals.
Only bank daybooks can have their own currency, yet miscellaneous, bank and financial postings have no currency field, so these journals are returned as not accepting other currencies.

not_mappable: unallocated_account: Horus has no suspense account per daybook or folder; always empty.
blocked: no Horus flag; derived from the daybook type, reflecting what the API can post.
next_document_numbers: no API field exposes a next number per daybook (Horus can auto-number confirmed operations, but the sequence is not readable); empty by default (the Chift default).

routes.how_it_works: The connector checks that the number is free, creates the account with number and name, then reads it back, because Horus returns only an id. The Chift type is not sent: Horus accounts have no writable type or category.
routes.documented: accounts.new takes FolderId, SearchKey (the account number) and Heading (the name) and returns only the new Id. accounts.info returns the stored account with its Inactive flag and categories. Neither create nor update accepts a category or type.
depends_on_assumption: The returned type is computed from Horus data and number prefixes; a new account often comes back as 'other' or a prefix-based guess.
The duplicate check may miss an inactive account: whether accounts.list returns inactive accounts is undocumented.
needs_confirmation: Horus: does accounts.new derive a category from the number, and can a category be set at all (H12)?
Horus: account number rules per Belgian or Luxembourg chart, and the duplicate-number error (H7).
Chift: when the type cannot be stored, reject, warn or drop it silently (C3)?
routes.feasibility_reason: Creating an account with number and name is documented end to end, but the type cannot be written and the type returned is the same estimate as in the chart of accounts; number rules and the type policy are open (H12, H7, C3).

considerations.text: No endpoint deletes or renumbers an account, so an account created with a wrong number must be cleaned up manually in Horus Office.
The search key, 'usually the account number', is how every posting endpoint references an account, so the Chift number is the join key across routes.
The Chift type sent is lost; consumers that classify accounts by type see a computed type, e.g. 'other' until a bank journal uses the account.
Horus documents no number rules (length, classes per chart), so an invalid number is caught only by Horus, with an undocumented error.

not_mappable: type: no writable type or category in Horus; the type sent is lost and the type returned may differ.
scheme_ids: no reporting-scheme classification in Horus; always empty.

horus_support: POST /account-histories.list (VAT and cash typing, filter only)
routes.how_it_works: One Horus call returns the chart (number, name, active flag, categories; whether inactive and title accounts are included is undocumented, H12); the connector caches it and applies the class filter and paging itself. Horus has no account type, so the Chift type and type filter rely on a value computed from several Horus sources.
routes.documented: accounts.list returns number, name, Inactive flag and category fields per account; it filters only by number prefix and name, without paging. Bank and financial daybooks reference their account, and ledger lines carry an account type (customer, supplier, general, VAT, cash).
depends_on_assumption: The type is computed from journals, categories and ledger lines; the last fallback, Belgian number prefixes, is general accounting knowledge, not Horus documentation.
type=vat and type=cash are best effort: unused VAT or cash accounts are typed only by Belgian prefixes, not at all in Luxembourg.
The class filter assumes the search key is the account number, which the guide says is 'usually' the case.
needs_confirmation: Horus: full list of IntCategory codes, and is AccountCategory always filled, which would make the type reliable (H12)?
Chift: when a type filter can only be estimated, return 400, ignore it, or return a best-effort result (C18)?
Chift: meaning of other_expense and other_financial, to map Horus subcategories to the right type.
not_concluded: Whether the chart includes inactive and non-postable title accounts: no filter exists and the documentation is silent (H12).
routes.feasibility_reason: Number, name and active status are native; the account type, which consumers use to find bank, VAT or cash accounts, rests on a chain of estimates.

considerations.text: Customers and suppliers are not separate ledger accounts: they are usually booked on shared collective accounts (e.g. 400000, 440000) with a partner reference.
Horus recommends loading reference data once and caching it per folder; with no paging in Horus, every Chift page is cut from that full list.
Bank accounts linked to a bank journal are typed reliably; VAT, cash and payable types are less reliable for accounts without movements.

not_mappable: type: no account-level field; only a computed value, which can be wrong for accounts without movements.
scheme_ids: no Horus equivalent; always empty.

routes.how_it_works: One Horus call lists every folder the connected user can access (a Horus folder is one company's books, the Chift folder); Chift adds its 'selected' flag from activation. Proposal: the address country, one extra call per folder, is left empty by default.
routes.documented: folders.list returns id, name, legislation (BE or LU), VAT liability, VAT number and address for the folders the user can access; CountryCode comes only from folders.info. API visibility follows the user's access in Horus.
depends_on_assumption: main_currency is returned as 'EUR': Horus folders have no currency field (H4).
active is always true for returned folders (no Horus status); a selected folder that disappears is returned as inactive.
company_number is derived from a Belgian VAT number (general knowledge), empty otherwise; street and house number are split from one address string.
needs_confirmation: Horus: is a folder's base currency always EUR (H4)?
Horus: does folders.list return archived or closed folders, and is the enterprise number available anywhere?
Chift: is the address country needed, given its cost of one extra call per folder (C4)?
routes.feasibility_reason: Id, name, VAT number and address come natively from one call; main_currency, active and company_number are assumptions because Horus folders carry no such fields.

considerations.text: A Horus folder is one company's books (the Chift folder); a Horus 'company' is a customer, supplier or beneficiary, i.e. a legal entity the folder deals with, not the folder's own company.
For an accounting firm, the list can hold every folder of its licence, so the activation picker may need search or filtering.
One Horus authorisation covers every folder the user can access, so Chift's folder selection at activation limits a connection's scope.
Each licence has its own API address and tokens, so one Chift connection covers one licence; a firm with several licences needs several connections.

not_mappable: Folder status: no active or archived flag; active is inferred from presence in the list.
main_currency: no Horus field; 'EUR' by assumption.
Address box number: no Horus field; always empty.

routes.how_it_works: The connector posts one balanced entry in the miscellaneous-operation daybook: signed Chift amounts become debits or credits, line types become customer, supplier or general. Journal, analytic codes and closed periods are checked first; the entry is read back only if Horus numbers it.
routes.documented: Lines carry a type (customer, supplier, general), account code, non-negative debit or credit, partner id where needed and optional analytics; debits must equal credits. Number is numeric; automatic numbering needs Confirmed = true. Only unconfirmed API entries can be deleted.
depends_on_assumption: Proposal (C15, H4): foreign-currency operations are converted to EUR at the supplied rate, as Horus operations have no currency field; folder currency assumed EUR.
Proposal (C7, C1): operation_number is the Horus entry number (non-numeric rejected); review mode pushes unconfirmed, direct mode confirms 'posted' operations.
Only Type 600 daybooks are accepted; other miscellaneous daybook types have no documented API posting path.
needs_confirmation: Chift: does Chift core convert foreign-currency amounts first, in which rate direction, and who absorbs rounding (C15)?
Chift: review or direct posting by default (C1), and is operation_number the entry number or a client reference (C7)?
Horus: may every user confirm entries (H21); is the entry number unique per daybook and year, and what happens on a duplicate (H3)?
not_concluded: Whether a VAT closure also blocks miscellaneous operations: fiscal years carry both closure dates and the guide is silent (H14).
Behaviour with several mandatory analytic plans, since Chift sends at most one analytic account per line (H13).
routes.feasibility_reason: Posting a balanced EUR operation is documented, but status mapping (C1, H21), foreign-currency conversion (C15) and numbering (C7) need answers first.

considerations.text: Horus keeps API entries unconfirmed by default for accountant review, while Chift defaults to 'posted'; which applies is a Chift decision (C1).
A confirmed operation cannot be deleted through the API; an unconfirmed one pushed through the API can.
An update creates a new entry with a new id, so consumers should reconcile on journal and number, not the id alone.
No idempotency key is documented, so a timed-out create is checked before any retry; the check works only when a number was supplied.

not_mappable: Original currency and rate: operations store EUR only, so the source currency cannot be read back.
Alphanumeric operation numbers: Horus numbers are numeric, so such references cannot be stored as the entry number.

routes.how_it_works: A Horus cost schema is an analytic dimension, the Chift analytic plan; one call returns all of them, at most eight per folder. The connector maps each list-type schema to a plan and cuts the page itself.
routes.documented: cost-schemas.list returns id, code, name, type (List or Free) and MasterCostSchema for every schema of the folder. A folder can use up to 8 cost schemas. Analytics depend on the folder's analytics module (WithAnalytics).
depends_on_assumption: parent_id is taken from MasterCostSchema; whether 'master' means a parent plan is undocumented.
Proposal (C9): Free-type schemas, which have no list of values, are not returned in v1.
Proposal: a folder without the analytics module returns an empty list, not an error.
needs_confirmation: Chift: list or hide Free-type dimensions, which have no enumerable analytic accounts (C9)?
Horus: what MasterCostSchema means, and what cost endpoints return for a folder without analytics (H13).
routes.feasibility_reason: One documented call returns every required plan field, but parent_id rests on an undocumented field (MasterCostSchema), and hiding Free-type schemas is a proposal pending C9.

considerations.text: Horus calls analytics 'cost' analytics: a plan is a cost schema (e.g. DEPARTMENT), an analytic account is a cost section (e.g. OFFICE).
Free-type dimensions take free text, digits or dates instead of a list of values, so they do not fit Chift's plan-and-account model.
Proposal: the plan id is the Horus schema GUID; Horus posts by schema code, so write routes translate the id through a cached lookup.

not_mappable: Plan active status: cost schemas have no active flag; always returned as active.
Plan code, description and mandatory flag: no Chift field, so users cannot see that a dimension is mandatory.

routes.how_it_works: Horus lists cost sections one schema at a time, so the connector reads the schemas, calls the section list once per list-type schema (at most eight) and merges them into one Chift page. Inactive sections are requested explicitly, since the Chift route returns all accounts.
routes.documented: cost-sections.list requires FolderId and CostSchemaId and returns id, code, name, Inactive flag and parent schema per section. Inactive sections are left out unless IncludeInactive is set. Only List-type schemas hold cost sections.
depends_on_assumption: Proposal (C4): balance, credit and debit are returned empty rather than 0, since Horus stores no balance and 0 would read as real.
needs_confirmation: Chift: balances empty, 0, or computed over the current fiscal year, on confirmed entries only or all (C4)?
Horus: is a section code unique per folder or only per plan? The guide and posting reference differ (H7).
Horus: meaning of IsLocked and IsDefault on a section, and should locked sections show as inactive (H13)?
not_concluded: Computed balances: sign and response shape of cost histories are undocumented, and unconfirmed entries cannot be excluded there.
Whether child sections appear at top level in the section list; the hierarchy has no Chift field.
routes.feasibility_reason: Listing every analytic account of every plan is documented, via a loop over at most eight plans; only computed balances, if Chift wants them (C4), remain open.

considerations.text: One Chift call needs up to nine Horus calls (schema list plus one section list per plan), so results are cached per folder, as Horus recommends.
Horus stores no balance per analytic account; balances exist only as period totals of analytic lines, and the Chift route carries no period.
Proposal: the analytic account id is the Horus section GUID; Horus posts by code, so write routes translate ids through the same cached list.
Section lists have no 'modified after' filter, so a section created or deactivated in Horus Office appears only after the cache refreshes.

not_mappable: balance, credit, debit: not stored per account; computable only over a period the route does not carry.
currency: cost sections have none; empty unless balances are computed, then EUR by assumption.
Section hierarchy and categories: no Chift field; the list is flattened.

routes.how_it_works: Clients: the open sales invoices list gives each open invoice or credit note with a native open amount, joined with customers.outstanding for account and matching. Suppliers: with no purchase equivalent, open items come from suppliers.outstanding ledger lines, amounts computed from debit and credit.
routes.documented: The guides name these three as the open-item endpoints (lines 'not matched yet'). The sales list gives total, open amount, invoice currency and due date; the ledger lists give open lines with debit, credit and matching, but no open amount.
depends_on_assumption: Without a company filter, the lists return every partner's open items, complete and uncapped (H8).
Proposal (C5): positive means owed, credit notes and payments negative; supplier open amount equals the line amount, partly matched groups netted if returned.
Proposal (H4, C16): supplier items in EUR at rate 1, client items in invoice currency; reference read from the line comment (H9).
needs_confirmation: Horus: do the ledger lists cover all partners without a company filter, and return partially matched lines (H8)? Ledger currency and rate direction (H4)?
Horus: volume limits and timeouts for whole-folder reads (H5); do SumDebit/SumCredit cover exactly the returned lines (H23)?
Chift: sign convention and partial-match allocation (C5); one item per due date or invoice, and unallocated payments (C17); unposted payments (C10).
not_concluded: Carried-forward items: IsReport is undefined and no link to the original exists, so original_document stays null. An item might also appear twice (prior-year and carry-forward line), overstating open items. Guard: a ledger line of an entry already kept from the open sales list is never emitted again; test on a folder spanning a year-end (H8).
Whether the debit/credit signs in the documented examples are real; the supplier example shows a debit on a supplier line.
How partially paid supplier invoices behave if Horus omits partly matched lines; a test-folder check must choose the fallback.
routes.feasibility_reason: Client open items are native, but folder-wide completeness and supplier open amounts depend on undocumented partial-matching behaviour Horus must confirm (H8).

considerations.text: The two sides differ: clients get a native open amount from Horus, while supplier open amounts are computed by the connector from ledger lines.
No date, paging or modified-after filter: every request reads all open items of the folder and the connector pages them.
Unconfirmed entries (the Horus default and the proposed review mode) count as unposted until confirmed, so they appear only with unposted_allowed=true.

Item ids are ledger line ids, expected to change when the source entry is updated; matching numbers appear to be numbered per partner (the next-number endpoints take a company), so they are not assumed unique per folder.

not_mappable: Supplier amounts in invoice currency: ledger lines carry a currency code and rate but no separate foreign amount, and the currency of Debit/Credit is undocumented (H4). Proposal: EUR at rate 1 until H4 is answered.
Several due dates and payment methods per item: Horus has one due date per line and no readable payment method.
original_document.id for carried-forward items: no link to the prior-year document; null.
journal_type is per journal: a credit note in a sales journal shows as customer_invoice; the sign tells them apart.

client.intro: On Horus, Create client becomes POST /companies.new in the Horus folder. A Chift client is a Horus "company": the one third-party record of a folder, flagged as customer and/or supplier. Most identity, contact and address fields copy across directly or with light formatting. The connector fills the Horus-required fields that Chift does not send (search key, role flags, VAT liability, language, country) by rule. Horus returns only the new id, so the Chift response is built by reading the record back.
call_flow: Reference data, cached per folder: GET /folders.info (default language and country), POST /accounts.list (checks account_number exists and is active), POST /countries.list (checks the country code).

Pre-checks with POST /companies.list (proposal): search by VAT number and by external reference, so a duplicate gets a clear Chift error or a hint to use force_merge. Then search by the generated search key to make sure the code is free in the folder.
Create with POST /companies.new: FolderId, generated SearchKey, role flags, one address, contact data and the IBANs in the same call. Horus returns only the new Id.

When force_merge is set, these calls replace step 3. GET /companies.info confirms the id is a supplier in the same folder. POST /companies.update sets IsCustomer = true. POST /ibans.new adds any IBAN not yet stored.

Read back in two to three calls. GET /companies.info gives the stored values, the last-modified date and the search key. POST /ibans.list gives the IBANs and BICs. The receivable account number comes from the cached chart, or from GET /accounts.info.
Build the Chift response from what was read back, using the same partner rules as the invoice routes (proposal): one 'main' address, is_company = true, and null for fields Horus does not store.

rows.note: Points to the Chift connection that holds one Horus licence's API address and tokens. Each Horus licence has its own database and endpoint. Not sent to Horus as data.

rows.horus_field: FolderId (companies.new body; also on every folder-scoped check)
rows.note: A Chift folder is a Horus folder ('the accounting record of one company'). If folder_id is absent, the single selected folder is used (Chift rule). With several folders and none given, the call returns 400. Who enforces the selection: C12.

rows.horus_field: CompanyId on companies.update (IsCustomer = true) + ibans.new; companies.new is skipped
rows.note: Horus keeps customer and supplier in one record, so the existing supplier is flagged as customer instead of duplicated. Proposal: check it is a supplier in this folder, fill only empty fields, never overwrite its VAT number or reference (C6).
Same meaning, required on both sides. Also the basis for the generated search key (proposal). Horus documents no maximum length.

Horus recommends this field for the integrator's own identifier, so the company can be found again reliably. Proposal: also use it for the duplicate check. Whether Horus keeps it unique is undocumented (H7).
Horus has no company/individual flag: every third party is a 'company' record. Business impact: an individual is stored as a company and comes back as one.

A Horus company has no person-name fields. The FirstName/LastName on beneficiaries are for payroll payees and must not be used. Proposal option: put first + last name in ContactPerson, whose meaning is to confirm (H11).
Not stored, same as first_name. An individual's name survives only inside name.
Horus has no job-title field. The value is dropped, so the client application must keep it.
Horus has no link from a person to a parent company. Proposal: ignore the value, or reject it if Chift prefers strict behaviour (C3).

The ISO code is upper-cased (fr → FR). The Horus company list is FR, NL, DE, EN, ES, PT, XX. Proposal: any other value, or none, gets the folder language because Horus requires one. The original value is then lost.
Proposal: active = false sets CustomerActivitySuspended = true. Horus gives this field no description, so its meaning must be confirmed before relying on it (H11).

key_points.text: One record holds both roles, which is why force_merge maps cleanly: the existing supplier is flagged as customer instead of being duplicated.

One Chift call needs several Horus calls. Horus create calls return only an id, so the company, its IBANs and (unless cached) its receivable account are read back to build the Chift response. That is two to three extra calls, and about three to seven in total with the checks. Rate limits are undocumented (H5).

Horus requires a search key, role flags, a VAT-liability flag, a language and a country that Chift may not send. The search key is the main business choice, because it becomes the client's code that accountants see. Proposal: generate it from the name. The convention is to agree with Chift (C8) once Horus states the rules (H7).

Some data cannot be stored: extra addresses, mobile, notes, person fields, job title, company link, client currency, non-IBAN bank accounts, and the enterprise number of VAT-liable clients. Individuals come back as companies. Client applications must keep this data on their side. Whether to reject or drop such input is a Chift decision (C3).

Duplicates: by default Horus refuses a VAT number that is already used, and it documents no idempotency key. Proposal: search by VAT number and external reference before creating, and never retry blindly after a timeout. Without either value there is no reliable duplicate check (C8).

Still open for this route: the merge policy (C6), the error codes (C20), the meaning of the 'suspended' flag used for active (H11), and a test folder (H17). Writes go to real data, and the API has no call to delete a company.

client.coverage_check: Checked against appendix_chift_spec_extract.md (POST /consumers/{consumer_id}/accounting/clients), not only against create_client.json. Path and query parameters: consumer_id, folder_id and force_merge each have a row. ClientItemIn: all 21 attributes have a row each (external_reference, first_name, last_name, name, function, is_company, company_id, phone, mobile, email, language, internal_notes, website, vat, company_number, iban, bank_account, currency, active, addresses, account_number). AddressItemIn: all 11 attributes have a row each (address_type, name, number, box, phone, mobile, email, street, city, postal_code, country). Response (ClientItemOut, AddressItemOut, BankAccountsItem, RoutingCodeItem): only fields that are not a plain read-back of the request get their own row (id, last_updated_on, third_party_account, account_number, is_company, language, active, company_number, currency). Deliberately grouped: the bank_accounts[] subfields in one row; the deprecated iban and bank_account in one row; the AddressItemOut subfields in one row; the six fields always returned as null in one row; name, vat, external_reference, phone, email and website in one 'read back from Horus' row. A ChiftError row covers the 400/422 responses the contract declares. Chift error-code names that appear in create_client.json are left out, because they are not in the spec extract.

invoice.intro: On Horus, a Chift sale or purchase entry becomes a book entry created by invoices.sales.new (customer invoices and refunds) or invoices.purchases.new (supplier invoices and refunds), with the PDF in the same call. Most header and line amounts map directly. The work is in four areas: resolving references (folder, daybook, company, accounts, analytic dimensions), turning each Chift tax code into a Horus VAT combination, converting analytic percentages into amounts, and deciding what to do with Chift fields that Horus cannot store.
call_flow: Reference data, cached per folder: daybooks.list to pick or check the sales/purchase daybook, accounts.list to check line accounts, cost-schemas.list and cost-sections.list to turn analytic ids into the search keys Horus posts with, and folders.info for the folder legislation (BE/LU), which selects the VAT list. fiscal-years.list is read fresh before each create, because the accountant can close a period at any time.

Partner: companies.info checks that partner_id belongs to the folder and has the customer or supplier role. Without partner_id, companies.list finds the company from partner_info and companies.new creates it if it is missing (proposal). Horus needs a CompanyId before it accepts an invoice.

Duplicate check: book-entries.list filtered on the document number. Horus has no idempotency key and the API has no invoice delete, so this check runs before the create and before any retry (proposal, best effort).
Create: invoices.sales.new for customer_* or invoices.purchases.new for supplier_*, with the PDF in the same call. Horus returns only the new entry Id.

Read-back, skipped when ignore_accounting_id=true: book-entries.info by Id gives the stored number, confirmation status and last-update date. account-histories.list is added only when line-level data is needed, such as the EUR amount of a foreign-currency invoice or the partner's collective account.
