key_points.text: One Chift call becomes several Horus calls. Before posting, Horus needs the folder, the daybook, the company and the search keys of accounts and analytic dimensions. Its create call returns only an id, so the Chift response is rebuilt from the request plus a read-back.

VAT is the main gap. Chift sends one tax_code per line, but Horus accepts no VAT code: it takes a combination of rate, origin and type (plus three purchase fields), valid only as listed in Horus's BE/LU spreadsheets. Proposal: a connector-owned VAT-code list per folder. Horus must confirm the files are current (H1), and Chift must accept the approach (C2).

Posting status and numbering need Chift decisions. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, while Chift defaults to 'posted'. Horus invoice numbers are numeric, and invoices have no automatic-numbering option. Proposal: review mode by default, and Number 0 (returned as draft) when no number is sent (C1, C7).

Some fields cannot be mapped: withholding tax, the Dutch G/N split, accrual dates, a forced period or a delivery date in another month, payment terms, and line quantity, unit price and unit. reference survives only inside the comment. Rejecting these inputs or silently dropping them is a Chift product decision (C3), because the create response has no warnings field.

Analytics change shape. Per-plan percentages must become amounts on combinations of up to 8 dimensions. Multi-plan splits assume the plans are independent (C9), and small lines may read back with slightly different percentages.

There is no undo. The API has no invoice delete, and an update creates a new entry with a new id, so a duplicate or wrong invoice cannot be removed through the integration. Hence the number check before any retry (best effort) and the need for a test folder during development (H17).

invoice.coverage_check: A script extracted every path and query parameter and every request attribute of this operation from appendix_chift_spec_extract.md and matched them against the row names, with nothing missing. That covers 6 parameters (consumer_id, folder_id, force_financial_period, regroup_lines, ignore_accounting_id, force_currency_exchange), the 28 top-level attributes of InvoiceItemInMultiAnalyticPlans, and 29 nested leaf attributes: WithholdingTax 3, InvoiceCorrection 4, NlPaymentTermsSplit/PaymentTermAccountInfo 4, AccountToCreate 2, InvoiceLineItemInMultiAnalyticPlans 12, AnalyticDistribution 2, AnalyticDistributionDetail 2. Some containers are grouped on purpose: withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split (with g_account and n_account) and analytic_accounts[] are covered by their leaf rows. invoice_correction, partner_info, lines[] and analytic_distribution keep their own rows because the object itself drives a mapping. For nested fields, 'required' means required within the optional parent object, as in the Chift spec. On the response side, only fields that are not simply echoed get a row. The rest sits in the 'Other response fields' row and in two grouped rows (partner_id + journal_id; payment_term_id + delivery_date + withholding_tax).

outst.intro: The route returns the open (unpaid or unallocated) items of a folder's customers or suppliers. Horus has open-item lists for both sides, but they are not symmetric. Client items come from the open sales invoices list, which has a native open amount, joined with customer ledger lines. Supplier items are rebuilt by the connector from supplier ledger lines. Each Chift item is therefore assembled from two or three Horus sources, and the connector or Chift handles signs, currency and paging.
call_flow: POST /daybooks.list (cached per folder): gives each journal's id, code and type. This feeds journal_id and journal_type, because supplier lines carry only the journal code.

type=client: POST /invoices.sales.outstanding.list for the whole folder (ConfirmedOnly when unposted_allowed=false). Returns open sales invoices, credit notes and linked payments with open amount, due date, invoice-currency amounts and payment remark.
type=client, in parallel: POST /customers.outstanding with no company filter. Returns customer ledger lines, joined on the line id to add account number, matching number and line comment.
type=supplier: POST /suppliers.outstanding with no company filter. Returns supplier ledger lines; the connector computes amount and open amount (Credit − Debit) and filters on Confirmed itself.

Chift side: remove payments that appear twice, apply filters, sort, return the requested page and count the total. Optional, off by default (Proposal): GET /book-entries.info per entry for the supplier payment communication and carried-forward details.

rows.note: Identifies the Chift connection. Chift uses it to find the stored Horus licence URL and tokens. Nothing is sent to Horus.
Horus documents no paging, so the connector fetches the full open-item set, sorts it and returns the requested page. Speed on large folders is unverified (H5).
Page size of the emulated pagination (default 50). It does not change the Horus calls, which always return the whole set.
Same concept: a Horus folder is the accounting record of one company. If omitted, the single folder selected at activation is used, as Chift's own folder rule states.
Chooses the Horus endpoints. Clients need two lists (open sales invoices plus customer ledger lines); suppliers have only ledger lines. Employee open items are not covered.
false keeps only accountant-confirmed entries: a native filter on the sales list, a connector filter on ledger lines. Whether unconfirmed payments still reduce open amounts depends on C10.
Proposal: one item per open customer or supplier ledger line. A linked payment that Horus lists twice is kept once. Instalments and unallocated payments are open questions (C17).
Computed by Chift: number of items after filtering and de-duplication, counted on the full set fetched from Horus.
Echo of the requested page.
Echo of the requested page size.
The ledger line id, the unit that Horus matching works on. Not stable: updating the source invoice creates a new entry, so the id presumably changes.
Converted to text. 0 (an unconfirmed entry without a number) becomes null. Uniqueness scope is undocumented (H3); read numbers together with journal_id.
Clients: the daybook id is on the row. Suppliers: Horus gives only the journal code, so the id is looked up in the cached daybook list.

rows.horus_field: Type (daybooks.list), reached through the item's daybook
rows.note: Proposal: a shared daybook-type table (sale → customer_invoice, sale credit note → customer_refund, bank → financial_operation…). It describes the journal, so a credit note keyed in a sales journal reads customer_invoice (H2).
Date part of the Horus date-time, with no time-zone conversion. Preferred over AccountingMonth/AccountingYear; Horus describes neither field.
Date-time converted to a date. On the sales list Horus fills it only for invoices and credit notes, so payments come back with null.
Horus has one due date per ledger line, so the list has zero or one element. Several instalments become several items (question C17).
Same value as items[].due_date.

rows.horus_field: — (invoice PaymentMode can be written but not read)
rows.note: Returned null. Horus accepts a payment mode when an invoice is created, but no read endpoint returns it, so payment apps cannot see the expected payment method.
Returned null, for the same reason as payment_method.
Proposal: equals open_amount (remaining amount due), since each item has one due date. Use amount instead if Chift means the scheduled instalment amount.
Proposal: open sales invoices keep their own currency. Supplier and other ledger lines are returned in EUR, because Horus gives no foreign-currency amount for them. Depends on H4 and C16.

rows.horus_field: TotalAmount / TotalCurrencyAmount (invoices.sales.outstanding.list); constant 1 for EUR items
rows.note: Proposal: 1 for every euro item. For foreign-currency sales rows, computed from the two amounts Horus returns. The direction of Horus's own CurrencyRate is undocumented (H4).

rows.horus_field: TotalAmount / TotalCurrencyAmount (invoices.sales.outstanding.list); Debit − Credit (customer lines); Credit − Debit (suppliers.outstanding)
rows.note: Proposal: positive = owed (invoice +, credit note and payment −). Horus documents no sign rule: clients are signed from the transaction type, suppliers use Credit − Debit. Depends on C5 and H2.

rows.horus_field: OpenAmount / OpenCurrencyAmount (invoices.sales.outstanding.list); computed from Debit, Credit, MatchDetail (suppliers.outstanding)
rows.note: Clients: documented Horus open amount. Suppliers: Horus has no open amount, so the line amount of unmatched lines is used. Partially paid supplier invoices depend on H8 (Proposal: net per matching group).
Horus company id, Horus's term for a customer or supplier. A line without a counterparty cannot be returned because partner_id is required (Proposal: skip and log it).

rows.horus_field: AccountSearchKey (customers.outstanding, joined on line id; suppliers.outstanding)
rows.note: Suppliers: on the line. Clients: the sales list has no account, so it comes from the joined customer ledger line. Horus search keys are 'usually the account number'.
One-element list when matched, otherwise empty. Horus appears to number matchings per customer or supplier, so values are unique only with partner_id (question C17).
Proposal: Horus Confirmed (accountant-confirmed) is read as Chift posted; the sources do not equate the two. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default.

Proposal: the first non-empty value of the ledger-line comment, then the sales remark, keeping the part before ' | ' (invoice-creation convention). Where Horus shows the invoice comment is undocumented (H9).
Clients: Horus payment remark (e.g. a structured communication). Suppliers: not on the supplier list, so null in v1. Proposal: an optional per-entry read, off by default.
Meant for items carried forward from an earlier year. Horus flags such lines (IsReport) but does not define the flag. Null in v1 (Proposal) until Horus defines IsReport (H8).
Horus documents no link from a carried-forward line to the prior-year line. Always null, so consumers cannot trace the original item by id.

rows.chift_field: items[].original_document.number, journal_id, journal_type, date, due_date, reference
rows.horus_field: DocumentNo, DaybookSearchKey, Date, DueDate, Comment of the carried-forward line
rows.note: Null in v1; could be read from the carried-forward line once Horus defines IsReport (H8, H9).

horus_required_extra.how_filled: From folder_id. If folder_id is omitted, the single folder selected at activation is used (Chift's own folder rule). With several selected folders, the request is rejected with 'folder_id required'.
The line id of an open sales row that is missing from the customer ledger list. Used to read that row's account number and matching number.
Proposal, off by default: the book entry id of a supplier or carried-forward line, to read its payment remark and entry type. One cached call per distinct entry.

key_points.text: Clients and suppliers are built differently. Clients get Horus's documented open amount. Horus has no open-amount list for suppliers, so the connector uses the amount of unmatched ledger lines. Whether partially paid supplier invoices appear at all depends on Horus (H8, a before-build question). If they do not, a fallback is needed that reads unmatched ledger lines over a period.
No loop per partner is needed, provided that leaving out the company filter returns every partner of the folder (to confirm, H8).

Horus documents no paging, so the connector fetches the full open-item set and pages it itself. Response time on large folders is unverified (H5), and keeping a short cache between page calls needs Chift's agreement (C14).

Not mappable or degraded: payment_method (Horus does not return it on read), original_document (carry-forward flag undefined; null in v1, Proposal), at most one due date per item, and supplier payment_communication (null by default). Horus credit-control data (reminder level, payment status, cash discount) has no Chift field. Item ids are expected to change when the source invoice is updated.

Signs and currency are connector proposals that still need agreement. Positive means owed, so credit notes and payments are negative (C5, H2). Open sales invoices keep their own currency and every other line comes back in EUR, so one customer's items can mix currencies (C16, H4).

With unposted_allowed=false, only entries confirmed by the accountant are returned. Entries pushed through the API are unconfirmed by default, so they stay out of that view until the accountant confirms them. Whether the connector can push them as confirmed is the posting-mode decision (C1).

outst.coverage_check: Checked against the Chift spec extract for GET /consumers/{consumer_id}/accounting/outstandings: 1 path parameter (consumer_id) plus 5 query parameters (page, size, folder_id, type, unposted_allowed); the ChiftPage envelope (items, total, page, size); the 18 OutstandingItem fields; the 4 OutstandingItemDueDatesOut fields; and the 7 OriginalOutstandingItem fields. That makes 39 rows, one per attribute, with none grouped, and matches the 39 field_mappings in data/outstandings.json. The extract does not list the enum values of OutstandingType or BoolParam, so 'client/supplier' and 'true/false' follow the route name and the analysis. One claim in the data file was softened: that a linked payment is returned both inside the invoice and as its own row. The appendix shows top-level payment rows and LinkedElements, but not the raw duplicated example, so the claim is stated as a deduction.

differences.chift: Clients and suppliers are separate resources. A client can be an individual (first and last name, is_company false) with several typed addresses, a mobile number and internal notes.
differences.horus: Each third party is one 'company', flagged customer and/or supplier. companies.new requires a search key (unique per folder), VAT liability, language and country. One address; no person, mobile or notes fields.
differences.why_it_matters: Client creation must generate a search key and fill fields Chift never sends; force_merge flags an existing supplier as customer. See limitation 8 (section 5).

differences.chift: Every invoice line requires tax_code, the id of a VAT code in the accounting software; GET vat-codes lists those codes.
differences.horus: No VAT-code list and no VAT code on write. Each line carries rate, origin and type (plus kind and condition on purchases), valid only as listed in two published spreadsheets. Reads return VatCode/VatHeading strings of undocumented meaning.
differences.why_it_matters: Proposal (C2): the connector owns a VAT-code list per folder legislation (BE/LU) and direction, decoding codes on write and rebuilding them on read. See limitation 1.

differences.chift: Invoices are documents (header, lines, type, status, payments, due dates), read by invoice_type. Journals carry a journal_type such as customer_invoice or customer_refund.
differences.horus: Posted invoices become book entries (headers, listed per daybook and month) and ledger lines. The daybook type decides the posting endpoint. Entries and ledger lines do not say invoice or credit note; only open sales invoices and credit notes are listed with their type (attached files also carry a type in documents.list/.info).
differences.why_it_matters: Invoice retrieval is rebuilt from several endpoints, telling invoices from credit notes rests on an assumption (H2), and supplier open amounts are computed from unmatched ledger lines. See limitations 4 and 5.

differences.chift: Per line and per plan, whole-number percentages totalling 100 % per plan. Miscellaneous operations take one analytic account per line.
differences.horus: Cost lines are amounts on combinations of cost sections (one per cost schema) and must sum exactly to the line base amount. A folder has at most 8 cost schemas; free-text dimensions (Free type) have no list of values.
differences.why_it_matters: Percentages must become amounts on combinations and back (Proposal, C9: a line split 60/40 between two departments and 50/50 between two projects becomes four department-project combinations of 30, 30, 20 and 20 %). Small amounts may read back with a slightly different split. Free-type dimensions are hidden (Proposal, C9).

differences.chift: status defaults to 'posted'. invoice_number is a free string, generated by the software when missing and recommended for idempotency; operation_number is a free string with no documented rules.
differences.horus: API entries are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them. Numbers are numeric and may be 0 only while unconfirmed. Automatic numbering works only on confirmed miscellaneous, bank and financial operations, not invoices.
differences.why_it_matters: Chift's default conflicts with Horus's review-by-default design, and numbers such as INV-2024/001 cannot be stored as the number: a posting-mode rule and a rule for unnumbered invoices are needed (C1, C7). See limitation 2.

differences.chift: A create returns the created object with its id (ignore_accounting_id may change the output).
differences.horus: A create returns only an Id. Updating an invoice or operation creates a new book-entry Id. No idempotency key is documented, and invoices, companies and accounts have no delete endpoint.
differences.why_it_matters: Every create needs a read-back and a best-effort duplicate check, and ids change after an edit, so consumers should reconcile on journal and number. See limitation 6.

differences.chift: Lists are paginated (page, size, total) and filtered by day-level dates, updated_after and type.
differences.horus: No list has paging parameters, and ledger reads take month periods. The API reference documents a "modified after" filter (ModifiedAfter) only on companies.list, book-entries.list and account-histories.list (the guide says "among others"). No deletion signal is documented.
differences.why_it_matters: The connector reads full results, emulates paging, totals and day filters, and needs periodic full re-syncs to catch deletions and replaced ids. See limitation 3.

differences.chift: One consumer connection, with folders selected at activation; requests to folders that were not selected must be rejected.
differences.horus: Each licence has its own database and API URL, returned at the end of OAuth. What the API shows depends on the authorising user's access. Endpoints that read or change one record by its id take no folder.
differences.why_it_matters: The API URL is stored per connection. Proposal: it is checked against a host pattern Horus confirms (H24) before Chift's client secret is sent to it. One grant appears to cover every folder the user can access (deduction), so the connector or Chift's platform must enforce the selected folders (C12), including on those id-only calls. Refresh tokens can be used only once, so two refreshes of one connection must never run at the same time; a temporary refresh error should not disconnect it (proposal).

limitations.title: VAT codes exist only as published tax combinations
limitations.what: Horus accepts no VAT code and has no VAT-code list. A line's rate, origin and type (plus kind and condition on purchases) must match a published combination. The API reference's value lists omit the Luxembourg origins used in the files, and the VAT kind is not returned on read.
limitations.implication: GET vat-codes and every tax_code become connector-owned data. Luxembourg and non-VAT-liable folders remain uncertain, some purchase codes come back empty on read, and codes missing from the files cannot be posted.
limitations.handling: Proposal: one VAT-code list per folder legislation (BE/LU) and direction, built from the files. Codes not on the folder's list are rejected before calling Horus; ambiguous codes return null on read. Fallback if Horus cannot confirm the files: start with a reduced VAT-code list.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus, on the files (H1); Chift, on the synthetic list and the VAT-amount policy (C2).
limitations.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes (dependency)

limitations.title: 'Posted' and numbering do not map one to one
limitations.what: API entries are unconfirmed by default, for accountant review. Numbers are numeric and may be 0 only while unconfirmed, and invoices have no automatic numbering. Whether every licence and user may confirm entries is undocumented.
limitations.implication: A 'posted' request may be stored as a draft. A sales invoice to be confirmed without a number cannot be posted as confirmed (purchases: undocumented, H3), and numbers such as INV-2024/001 are rejected. Unnumbered entries cannot be found again after an accountant edit.
limitations.handling: Proposal: a posting mode per connection, review (default; entries unconfirmed) or direct ('posted' confirmed), always reporting the status actually stored. An invoice without a number is pushed for review and returned as a draft; the printed number goes in reference.
limitations.decision_owner: Chift (C1, C7); Horus, on confirmation rights and numbering (H21, H3).
limitations.routes: Invoice creation, miscellaneous operation creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items

limitations.title: No documented paging, limits or timeouts
limitations.what: No Horus list has paging parameters, ledger reads are bounded by month, and no rate, size or time limit is documented. That lists return complete results is a deduction, not a documented fact.
limitations.implication: Without a cache, each Chift page may re-read the whole period. Behaviour on large accounting-firm folders, including any silent truncation, is unverified, and incremental polls still read ledger lines per period.
limitations.handling: Proposal: cache reference data per folder and results between page calls (C14), default invoice retrieval to the current fiscal year (C11), and run a volume test on the largest test folder. Fallback if volumes are a problem: make a date window mandatory on invoice retrieval.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus, on its limits (H5); Chift, on caching, timeouts and default windows (C14, C11).
limitations.routes: All list routes; most exposed: invoice retrieval, outstanding items

limitations.title: Invoices are rebuilt from the ledger, without the document type
limitations.what: No endpoint lists all invoices: invoices.sales.outstanding.list returns only open sales invoices and credit notes, without lines. Headers come from book-entries.list per daybook and period, lines from account-histories.list, and neither says invoice or credit note. The document type appears only on open sales items and on attached documents (documents.list/.info), so it cannot classify every entry.
limitations.implication: The most complex read route, with several Horus calls per request. A credit note keyed into a sales daybook, in a folder that also has a credit-note daybook, reads back as an invoice with negative amounts. Quantity and unit price are not stored.
limitations.handling: Proposal: the daybook type decides; the amount sign is used only in folders without a credit-note daybook; the open-items type serves as a consistency check, not an override. The rule stays an assumption until Horus exposes the type.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus on credit-note rules and the type on read (H2); Chift on acceptable misclassification (C5).
limitations.routes: Invoice retrieval; also outstanding items and journals

limitations.title: Supplier open amounts are computed, not read
limitations.what: Client open items come with a native open amount. Suppliers have only ledger lines from suppliers.outstanding. Whether partially matched lines are returned, and whether every supplier is returned without a company filter, is undocumented.
limitations.implication: If partially matched lines are missing, supplier balances silently drop partly paid invoices. This affects a Task B route.
limitations.handling: Proposal: an unmatched line is open for its full amount; partly matched groups are netted if Horus returns them; otherwise supplier ledger lines are read as a fallback. First test: one partly paid purchase invoice and one partly paid sales invoice.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus on completeness and partial matching (H8); Chift on signs and allocation (C5, C17).

limitations.title: No idempotency key, and ids change on update
limitations.what: A create returns only an Id, and no idempotency key is documented. Updating an invoice or operation creates a new Id. Invoices, companies and accounts cannot be deleted through the API.
limitations.implication: A timed-out create can leave a duplicate that cannot be deleted. Every create needs a read-back to build the Chift response. Ids stored by client applications stop working after an edit.
limitations.handling: Proposal: best-effort duplicate check before every create and any retry (VAT number, external reference, account or document number); never retry blindly; return an 'outcome unknown' error when the record has no key. Consumers should always send a number. Once Horus has returned an id, the request never ends in an error: if the read-back fails, the response is built from the request (operation_number null when Horus generated it) and the read-back is retried later, because a client retry could book a second entry that the API cannot delete.
limitations.decision_owner: Chift on the duplicate policy and errors (C6, C7); Horus on duplicates and commits after a timeout (H3).

limitations.title: Currency support differs by object
limitations.what: Invoices accept a currency code and rate when the folder allows currencies; miscellaneous-operation lines have no currency field. On read, ledger lines carry a currency code and rate, but whether their amounts are in EUR or in that currency is undocumented; separate invoice-currency amounts appear only on open sales items.
limitations.implication: Foreign-currency operations are stored in euro without their original currency. On read, under the proposed EUR reading of ledger amounts (until H4 is answered), a foreign-currency sales invoice switches to euro once paid, and purchase invoices come back in euro.
limitations.handling: Proposal: convert foreign-currency operations at the exchange rate that Chift's contract requires, rather than reject them; never pair euro amounts with a foreign currency code. Verify with one foreign-currency invoice in the test folder.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus on the currency of ledger amounts (H4); Chift on who converts and how currency is shown (C15, C16).
limitations.routes: Miscellaneous operation creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items, invoice creation (response)

limitations.title: Third-party master data is narrower than Chift's client
limitations.what: companies.new requires a search key, VAT liability, language and country; search-key rules beyond uniqueness are undocumented. A company holds one address and no person, mobile or notes fields, and a duplicate VAT number is refused by default.
limitations.implication: The connector invents the customer code that accountants see. Extra addresses and person fields are lost. A duplicate policy is needed, including for clients without a VAT number or external reference.
limitations.handling: Proposal: generate the search key from the name, with a numeric suffix on collision; keep the main address, else the invoice address; pre-check duplicates and return the existing id; use force_merge for existing suppliers.
limitations.decision_owner: Chift (C8, C3, C6); Horus on search-key rules and field meanings (H7, H11).

limitations.title: Testing runs on real data
limitations.what: Requests run against the licence's real database; write tests need a test licence or test folder, and no sandbox is documented. The registration and Quickstart pages were not available for this analysis.
limitations.implication: No assumption can be checked until Horus provides a test licence: VAT acceptance, credit notes, partial matching, currency and volumes. Test invoices and companies cannot be deleted through the API.
limitations.handling: Proposal: in the validation phase, register the integration, obtain a test licence and folder, and run a volume test. Go/no-go condition: no build without a test licence.
limitations.decision_owner: Horus, on registration and test access (H17, H19); Chift, on the go decision.

questions.question: Tax combinations: (a) Are the two published spreadsheets current and complete for BE and LU folders, and how are changes announced? (b) Which TaxOrigin list is authoritative, given that the LU files use origins outside the API reference enums, and does the API accept those codes? (c) Which combination does a folder that is not VAT liable send, and is PCT sent as 35 or as 0.35? (d) How is an invalid combination rejected? (e) Are VatCode and VatHeading on read stable, and does each correspond to exactly one combination?
questions.why: Decides whether the connector's VAT catalogue can serve every tax_code clients send, and whether purchase VAT codes can be returned on read. A negative answer triggers a reduced VAT-code list.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

questions.question: Credit notes: Can a credit note (Type 1) be posted in a 200/100 daybook, and an invoice in a 250/150 daybook? Can the invoice type be exposed on book-entries.list or account-histories.list? Must credit-note amounts be positive, and are negative lines or totals accepted on Type 0?
questions.why: Decides daybook selection and the sign rules on write, and the invoice/credit-note classification on read, which today is an assumption.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, journals, outstanding items

questions.question: Numbering and duplicates: Is Number unique per daybook and fiscal year, and is a duplicate rejected (with which error)? Is there an idempotency key, or an external reference that could serve as one? Can a create that timed out still be committed, and is a new entry listed as soon as the call returns? What happens to a confirmed invoice sent with Number 0, and could invoices get AutoGenerateNumber?
questions.why: Decides whether duplicate checks and retries are safe, and whether confirmed invoices sent without a number can be supported.

questions.question: Currency: For foreign-currency documents, in which currency are ledger Debit/Credit and book-entry totals expressed? In which direction is CurrencyRate given, and is the folder base currency always EUR? Does invoices.*.new read amounts in the invoice currency?
questions.why: If ledger amounts are in the document currency, the EUR assumption (H4) returns wrong amounts on every foreign-currency read.
questions.routes: Invoice retrieval, outstanding items, invoice creation, miscellaneous operations

questions.question: Volumes: Are there rate limits, timeouts, maximum result sizes or maximum period spans on list endpoints? Can a list result be truncated without warning?
questions.why: Paging is emulated over full results. The design is unverified on large accounting-firm folders, and silent truncation would corrupt Chift totals.

questions.question: Outstanding items: With CompanyIds omitted, do customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding return every partner's open lines, without a cap? Are partially matched lines (MatchStatus 0) returned, with every line of the group, and are Debit/Credit the original amounts or the open remainder? How is a carried-forward line linked to its original document?
questions.why: Decides whether supplier outstanding items, which the connector computes, are complete, and which call pattern the route uses.

questions.question: Confirmation rights: May every integration, licence and user type set Confirmed = true on invoices and operations, or can the accounting firm restrict it? Which actions are blocked once an entry is confirmed? Are unconfirmed entries included in balances and VAT returns?
questions.why: Decides whether the proposed direct posting mode (Chift 'posted' sent as confirmed) can be offered on every connection, and what 'draft' means for clients.

questions.question: Onboarding: (a) Is docs.horus-software.be authoritative, and is the apiary documentation linked in the case deprecated? (b) How is an integration registered (client id and secret, redirect URIs), and which user should authorise it for an accounting firm and for an SMB? (c) Can Chift get a test licence or test folder, and can test data be removed? (d) What happens to tokens when the authorising user leaves or authorises again?
questions.why: Every mapping rests on the current documentation, and the two versions were not compared. Nothing can be verified or built safely without a registered integration and a test licence.

questions.question: Posting mode and numbering: (a) Should the connector offer a posting mode per connection: review (entries pushed unconfirmed, proposed default) or direct ('posted' sent as confirmed), with the response always reporting the stored status? (b) An invoice without invoice_number: push it for review as a draft (proposed), reject it, or let the connector generate the next number? (c) Is rejecting non-numeric numbers acceptable, with the number shown to customers kept in reference?
questions.why: Chift's default 'posted' and free-text numbers collide with Horus's review-by-default design and numeric-only numbers. The answers fix the invoice and operation creation mappings and what clients see.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, miscellaneous operation creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items

questions.question: Caching and timeouts: Can a connector keep a per-folder reference cache and a short-lived result cache between page calls of the same request? What is the timeout of a synchronous request, and is there a background pattern for heavy reads?
questions.why: Without a cache between page calls, every Chift page re-reads the whole Horus period. This decides whether emulated paging is viable.

questions.question: Foreign-currency miscellaneous operations: Does Chift core convert the amounts to the journal currency before calling the connector, as the other_currencies_allowed description suggests, or must the connector convert? In which direction is the rate expressed, and how should a rounding residue be absorbed?
questions.why: Horus operation lines have no currency field. The answer decides where conversion happens and what the operation response returns.

questions.question: Signs: Do consumers send refund amounts as positive values, and can invoices have negative lines or a negative total? On outstanding items, should a customer credit note or an unallocated payment be negative (balance view, proposed) or positive (document view, as in invoice due dates)?
questions.why: Changes the sign rule in invoice creation and the amount mapping of outstanding items (both Task B). Without a decision, the same credit note is positive in invoice retrieval and negative in outstanding items.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, outstanding items

questions.question: VAT codes: Is a connector-owned catalogue with synthetic ids (for example S-21-0-0), one per folder legislation and direction, acceptable for GET vat-codes, with tax_code = null on read when the match is ambiguous? Should VAT amounts be booked as sent (OverrideTaxAmounts = true, proposed) rather than recalculated by Horus within one cent?
questions.why: Fixes the tax_code mapping of invoice creation (Task B) and the VAT-amount policy, since Horus has no VAT-code entity.
questions.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

questions.question: Partner codes: How should the Horus search key of a new client be generated: from the name (proposed), from external_reference, or with a per-consumer scheme? What does partner_info.account_number mean, a third-party code or a ledger account? When a code matches a partner with a different name, should the connector refuse (409) or reuse it with a warning?
questions.why: Horus requires SearchKey, Chift has no field for it, and accountants see the code. The Chift spec does not describe partner_info.account_number. Changes the client creation and invoice creation mappings (Task B); the Horus search-key rules (H7) constrain the answer.

confirmed.text: Each of the 11 routes has documented Horus endpoints for its core object and operation (create or list; invoices are listed as book entries and ledger lines) in the documentation reviewed; no route lacks a capability.
Invoice creation is native: invoices.sales.new and invoices.purchases.new post invoices and credit notes (Type 0/1) with VAT, analytics and the PDF in one call.
Client open items are native: invoices.sales.outstanding.list returns open sales invoices and credit notes with open amount and payment status.
Horus publishes the accepted VAT combinations in two spreadsheets (sales, purchases), each with BE and LU sheets, and folders.list returns each folder's legislation.
confirmed.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

confirmed.text: The write rules are documented, so the connector can check them before posting: totals equal base plus tax, cost lines sum to the line base, miscellaneous operations balance.

assumption.text: Horus lists return complete results for a folder and period, so paging, totals and day-level filters can be emulated. Deduced from the absence of paging parameters.
The VAT spreadsheets are current and complete, and the API accepts the Luxembourg tax origins that are missing from the API reference's value lists.
assumption.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

assumption.text: Invoice or credit note on read follows the daybook type; the amount sign decides only where no credit-note daybook exists. A proposed rule, not documented behaviour.
suppliers.outstanding without a company filter returns every supplier's open lines, partially matched ones included; otherwise a fallback read of supplier ledger lines is needed.
Ledger amounts on read are in the folder currency (EUR). Open sales items, which carry a total and a separate invoice-currency total, suggest it; no source states it.

confirmation.text: Horus, VAT and posting: whether the tax files are current and authoritative (H1), credit-note daybook rules and the document type on read (H2), numbering and duplicate numbers (H3).
confirmation.routes: Invoice creation, invoice retrieval, VAT codes

confirmation.text: Horus, reads: the currency of ledger amounts (H4), rate, size and time limits (H5), and whether the outstanding endpoints return partially matched lines for all partners (H8).
confirmation.routes: Invoice retrieval, outstanding items, all list routes

confirmation.text: Horus, access: integration registration and a test licence or folder (H19, H17), the allowed API addresses and connection lifecycle (H24), whether every user may confirm entries (H21), and which documentation version is authoritative (H20).
Chift, before build: posting mode and the rule for invoices without a number (C1, C7), caching and timeouts (C14), and who converts foreign-currency operations (C15).
confirmation.routes: Invoice creation, miscellaneous operation creation, all list routes

confirmation.text: Chift, Task B conventions: the synthetic VAT-code list (C2), sign conventions (C5) and partner codes (C8).
confirmation.routes: Client creation, invoice creation, outstanding items

not_concluded.text: Whether the list routes perform and stay complete on large accounting-firm folders: no limits are documented and no volume test has been run.
not_concluded.routes: All list routes, mainly invoice retrieval and outstanding items

not_concluded.text: Whether supplier open items are complete for partly paid invoices. This depends on H8, or on a fallback validated with test data.

Whether every VAT case can be expressed: the files have no variant for non-VAT-liable folders, Luxembourg uses origins missing from the API reference's value lists, and the partial-deduction percentage on purchases (condition PCT, e.g. 35 % on car costs) appears both as 35 and as 0.35 in the sources.

Whether incremental sync catches every change: ModifiedAfter is documented on three lists only, its coverage of matching and accountant edits is undocumented, and no deletion signal is documented (H10).
Whether the mapping holds for the apiary documentation the case links and for the live Chift reference: neither was compared, and no live request was sent.

corrections.reference_said: Section 1: "All eleven Chift routes in scope can be built on the Horus Software API, and none is blocked... Nine need workarounds that the connector can absorb". Tiles: 2 Supported, 9 Supported with workaround, 0 Not supported, 0 To confirm.
corrections.now: Section 1: the documentation rules out none of the 11 routes, but only 1 is confirmed (analytic accounts). Six rest on assumptions, and four (invoice retrieval, invoice creation, miscellaneous operations, outstanding items) need answers from Horus or Chift. Large-folder behaviour cannot be concluded for any list route.
corrections.why: "Can absorb" had no evidence: Horus documents no limits, and the reference's own large-folder row (section 7) is "To confirm". Its H1 also said invoice creation "cannot post valid VAT without" the tax files, which conflicts with an unqualified "none is blocked".

corrections.topic: Rating scale replaced; analytic plans and ledger accounts
corrections.reference_said: Section 2 verdicts: Supported = "One native Horus endpoint, plus cached reference data, serves the route with deterministic transformations"; Supported with workaround = "Feasible, but needs ... emulated filters, pagination or numbering". Section 4: analytic plans is "a 1:1 read of the cached schema list (supported, D11)".
corrections.now: Routes are rated by evidence, not effort: Confirmed, Feasible with assumptions, Needs confirmation or Not yet concluded, by their weakest material point. Analytic plans is Feasible with assumptions: parent_id rests on an undocumented field (MasterCostSchema), emulated paging is a deduction and hiding Free schemas is a proposal pending C9. Ledger account creation is Feasible with assumptions too, because the type it returns is the chart-of-accounts estimate. Folders is Feasible with assumptions.
corrections.why: On the reference's own definition, analytic plans was "Supported with workaround": Chift's analytic-plans route is paginated while cost-schemas.list is not, and Free-type schemas are hidden pending C9. Under the new scale, every route whose response rests on an interpretation of undocumented Horus data (parent_id, a computed account type, the folder currency) is rated Feasible with assumptions, without exceptions.

corrections.reference_said: Section 2 Sources lists "the accepted tax-combination spreadsheets" as "Not available". Section 8, H1: "Can you share the accepted tax-combination files for sales and purchases?"
corrections.now: Sections 1 and 4: both spreadsheets, linked from the Horus invoice pages, were analysed (sales 18 BE and 58 LU combinations; purchases 109 BE and 146 LU). Discrepancies with the API reference are flagged (Luxembourg origins missing from the reference's value lists, partial-deduction value shown as 35 and 0.35), and H1 asks Horus to confirm the files.
corrections.why: The invoices.sales.new and invoices.purchases.new pages state "The accepted tax combinations ... are available here". The files are linked from Horus's own reference, so they can be analysed directly rather than requested from Horus. Some sales origin labels also differ from the reference (origin 16).

corrections.reference_said: Section 7: "Miscellaneous operations: the request has no currency field, so non-EUR operations are rejected (derived; proposed default, see C3)." Section 1: "miscellaneous operations are EUR-only".
corrections.now: Sections 3 and 5 (limitation 7), Proposal: foreign-currency operations are converted to EUR at the supplied rate, not rejected; the original currency is not kept. Who converts (Chift core or the connector), the rate direction and rounding are a before-build Chift question (C15).
corrections.why: Chift's contract says the exchange rate "Must be filled in when creating the operation in another currency from the folder's default currency". Rejecting such operations contradicts that contract; Horus lacking a currency field calls for conversion, not refusal.

corrections.reference_said: Section 3 concept map: "Posted / draft | Confirmed true / false | ... | Documented". Reference appendix B, decision D12: "'draft' → unconfirmed; 'posted' → confirmed, with a per-consumer option to always push unconfirmed."
corrections.now: Sections 2 and 5, Proposal: a posting mode per connection, review by default (entries pushed unconfirmed for the accountant) or direct; the response reports the status actually stored. The pairing is a proposal, not documented. Whether every user may confirm entries is a before-build question (H21).
corrections.why: No source equates Chift 'posted' with Horus Confirmed. Horus pushes API entries unconfirmed so the accountant can review them, and invoices cannot be deleted through the API. The reference default would skip that review on every request sent with Chift's default status.

corrections.topic: Invoice or credit note on read
corrections.reference_said: Reference appendix B, decision D1: "On read, always scan both daybook types and classify each entry as invoice or credit note from the sign of the customer/supplier line; for open sales items, the documented TransactionType takes precedence."
corrections.now: Section 5, limitation 4 (Proposal; an Assumption pending H2): the daybook type decides; the amount sign only where no credit-note daybook exists; the open-items type is a check, not an override. Stated failure: a credit note keyed into a sales daybook, where a credit-note daybook exists, reads as an invoice.
corrections.why: Chift's due-date amount allows credit-direction amounts on customer invoices ("A negative amount represents credit on customer invoices and supplier refunds"), so sign-first would file them as refunds. TransactionType exists only on open sales items, so the override would reclassify a document once paid.

corrections.topic: Supplier open amounts and partial matching
corrections.reference_said: Section 4: "Supplier items come from supplier ledger lines, with the open amount computed from matching groups." Section 7: "Partial payments and instalments. | Open amounts come from matching groups."
corrections.now: Section 5, limitation 5: an unmatched supplier line is open for its full amount; partly matched groups are netted only if Horus returns them, otherwise a fallback read is needed. H8 is a before-build question, and completeness for partly paid invoices is not yet concluded.
corrections.why: Horus states that lines "not matched yet make up the outstanding items". MatchStatus has a "Partially" value, but nothing says partially matched lines are returned. If they are not, partly paid supplier invoices disappear without notice.

corrections.reference_said: Section 6 building block: "Duplicate protection | Search before create (VAT number, external reference, document number) and check before retrying after a timeout or server error, because Horus has no idempotency key."
corrections.now: Section 5, limitation 6: the check is best effort. It works only when the record has a key; when it has none (no number, or a client without VAT number or external reference), the connector returns an 'outcome unknown' error instead of retrying. Consumers should always send a number.
corrections.why: Horus documents no idempotency key and nothing on commits after a timeout (H3). Unconfirmed entries may carry Number 0, leaving nothing to search on, and a duplicate invoice cannot be deleted through the API.

corrections.topic: ModifiedAfter documented on three lists only
corrections.reference_said: Section 3 conventions (labelled Documented): "Many lists offer ModifiedAfter/ModifiedBefore for incremental synchronisation."
corrections.now: Sections 1 and 2: ModifiedAfter is documented in the API reference only on companies.list, book-entries.list and account-histories.list, and no deletion signal is documented. Incremental reads need periodic full re-syncs; whether they catch matching changes and accountant edits is not yet concluded (H10).
corrections.why: The guides say "Many lists also offer ModifiedAfter / ModifiedBefore filters", but in the API reference the filter appears only in those three request schemas. Accounts, daybooks, analytics and open-item lists must be re-read in full.

corrections.reference_said: Section 4, invoice creation: "invoice_number null: a draft gets Number=0. A posted sale gets max(DocumentNo)+1 from the same call (assumption, race risk) or is rejected. A posted purchase gets null (nullable)."
corrections.now: Sections 4 and 5, Proposal: an invoice without a number is pushed unconfirmed with Number 0 and returned as a draft; generating the next number is only an opt-in alternative (C7, H3). Non-numeric numbers are rejected, and the printed number goes in reference.
corrections.why: Horus allows Number 0 only while an invoice is unconfirmed and offers automatic numbering only for confirmed miscellaneous, bank and financial operations. A computed next number risks collisions, and an unnumbered entry has no key for duplicate checks.

corrections.reference_said: Section 3 concept map: "VAT code | No VAT-code entity: rate + origin + type ... | Documented". Section 5: "Horus VatDetail.VatCode is Horus's internal code and is never returned as the Chift tax_code".
corrections.now: Section 2: Horus has no VAT-code list and accepts no VAT code on write, but ledger reads return VatCode and VatHeading strings whose meaning is undocumented. tax_code is rebuilt from the line VAT fields (Proposal), and H1 asks what these codes represent.
corrections.why: account-histories.list/.info, customers.outstanding and suppliers.outstanding expose "VatCode: string|null" without a description; nothing shows it is internal. If it maps one-to-one to a combination, it could fill purchase tax_codes that now come back empty.

corrections.reference_said: Section 4, chart of accounts, items[].type ("the first match wins"): step 5 "ADispo ... → bank"; step 6 "'100: Assets' ... '600: Liability' ... → other"; step 7 BE fallback "411 or 451 → vat, 55 → bank, 57 → cash".
corrections.now: Section 3: chart of accounts is Feasible with assumptions. The type rests on a heuristic cascade, and type=vat and type=cash are best effort: ledger-line account types where the account has movements, Belgian prefixes otherwise, nothing for unused accounts in Luxembourg folders (C18).
corrections.why: With the first match winning, step 6 typed every account with a balance-sheet AccountCategory, VAT accounts included, as "other" before the BE fallback could run (unless the optional ledger-line step ran), and step 5 sent cash accounts to bank. Type=vat and type=cash filters returned almost nothing.

corrections.reference_said: Section 2 Sources: "Horus API reference | 72 endpoint pages, each with its OpenAPI definition (documentation dated 24 September 2026)". The host is not named, and the report never states that no live request was made.
corrections.now: Cover and appendix A: the case links the former apiary documentation; the analysis used docs.horus-software.be and the Chift contract bundled in SDK 0.6.16, without comparing versions or sending live requests. H20 asks Horus which documentation is authoritative.
corrections.why: The case links horussoftwareapi.docs.apiary.io. If endpoint or field names differ between the two versions, parts of the mapping may not match the documentation the case links. No allowed source shows whether they differ, so this is a disclosure, not a claim that the mapping is wrong.

corrections.reference_said: Miscellaneous operation call sequence: "Accept it only if Data.Folder.Id == FolderId and Data.Daybook.Id == DaybookId (D13); otherwise return 400 (not expected for an Id this call has just created in that folder)." Its edge cases cover a create that times out, not a read-back that fails after the create.
corrections.now: Section 5, limitation 6: once Horus has returned an id, the request succeeds. If the read-back fails or shows a mismatch, the response is built from the request, the failure is logged and the read-back is retried later; nothing is re-created.
corrections.why: An error invites a retry by the client or by Chift, which would book a second entry, possibly confirmed, that the API cannot delete. The record already exists once Horus has returned its id.

corrections.topic: Selected folders enforced on every route
corrections.reference_said: Client creation only: "reject with 400 if it is not among the folders selected at Chift activation". The other routes apply only the rule that folder_id is required when several folders are selected.
corrections.now: Section 2: a folder_id outside the activation selection is rejected on every folder-scoped route, unless Chift's platform already enforces it (C12).
corrections.why: One Horus authorisation covers every folder the user can access, so on an accounting firm's licence a wrong folder_id could reach another client's books.

corrections.reference_said: "SearchKey = account_number sanitised with Client creation's rules ... If the match lacks IsCustomer (customer_*) or IsSupplier (supplier_*), POST /companies.update with CompanyId + that flag only".
corrections.now: Section 4, invoice creation (proposal): account_number is used exactly as sent and a found company's name is compared with account_name (409 on a mismatch); a missing customer or supplier role is not added implicitly (C8).
corrections.why: A sanitised or truncated code can match the wrong third party, and an invoice booked to the wrong partner cannot be deleted through the API. Adding a role changes master data the accountant owns.

corrections.topic: Invoice amounts and VAT as issued
corrections.reference_said: Refund amounts sent as "absolute value" field by field; invoice_correction adds "BaseAmount = Δuntaxed, TaxAmount = Δtax ... Comment = 'Rounding correction'" for any difference; the lines[].tax_amount row that sends OverrideTaxAmounts=true is labelled Documented.
corrections.now: Proposal: a refund with negative totals is sign-flipped as a whole document and sent as Type 1; a correction line is added only within a tolerance agreed with Chift (C19, section 4); mixed-sign documents are rejected until H2 and C5 are answered; OverrideTaxAmounts=true is a proposal (C2, H22).
corrections.why: Field-by-field absolute values can turn a discount line into a charge, and an unlimited correction line would book real data errors on the correction account. Booking VAT as sent is a choice made on documented Horus fields, not documented behaviour.

corrections.reference_said: Section 1: "Proceed with a Horus connector covering all eleven routes, built on a small set of shared components... Before building, settle the open questions with Horus that change the design ... and get a test license". Section 9: "A Horus connector is feasible for the full scope".
corrections.now: Section 1: "Proceed to a short validation phase rather than a full build": a test licence and before-build answers first, then reference routes and simple creates, then invoice creation and operations; ledger-based reads wait for Horus's answers. A proposal for Chift's decision, not a commitment.
corrections.why: The reference committed to all eleven routes before any answer or test. Horus has no sandbox, limits are undocumented (H5), posting and numbering are client-visible Chift decisions (C1, C7), and the ledger-based reads carry most open questions.

questions.short: Are the Horus tax-combination spreadsheets current, complete and authoritative for Belgian and Luxembourg folders (they differ from the API reference in places), and how are changes announced? How is an invalid combination rejected, and what do the VAT codes returned on read represent? Also: which combination applies to a folder that is not VAT liable, is the partial-deduction value (PCT) sent as 35 or 0.35, is a country expected on Luxembourg OSS origins, and could the VAT kind be returned on read?
questions.why: Every invoice’s VAT translation and the VAT-code list depend on this catalogue.

questions.short: Can credit notes and invoices be posted in each other’s daybooks, and can the document type be exposed on read (today it exists only on open sales items and on attached documents)? Which signs apply to credit notes, and are negative lines or negative invoice totals accepted?
questions.why: Decides daybook choice and sign rules on write, and invoice versus refund classification on read.

questions.short: Is a document number unique per daybook and fiscal year, and how are duplicates detected and rejected? Is there an idempotency key or a safe way to retry after a timeout? How are invoices and operations numbered when sent without a number?
questions.why: Duplicate protection, safe retries after timeouts, and numbering of entries sent without a number.

questions.short: For foreign-currency documents, which currency are amounts in on create and on read, can original-currency amounts be recovered for paid and purchase invoices, which way is the rate quoted, and is the folder currency always EUR?
questions.why: Correct amounts on write and on read for every foreign-currency document.

questions.short: Are there rate limits, timeouts, or caps on result size or date range for list endpoints, given they have no paging? Could account histories be fetched for several companies in one call?
questions.why: Lists cannot be paged and some routes need one call per daybook; behaviour on large folders is unverified.

questions.short: Which error types can the API return (duplicates, closed period, invalid tax combination, unknown account), which status does an id from another folder return, and do create endpoints themselves refuse dates in closed periods?
questions.why: Precise errors for Chift consumers, safe retry rules, and whether the connector’s closed-period check is the only guard.

questions.short: What are the rules for company and account search keys, are cost-section keys and external references unique per folder, and does Horus generate a company search key when none is sent?
questions.why: The connector generates company search keys, validates account numbers and finds partners by external reference.

questions.short: Do the outstanding-item endpoints return every open item of all partners, uncapped and without duplicates, including partially matched and carried-forward items? Are amounts original or remaining, can one invoice carry several due dates, and is a purchase-side open-invoice list planned?
questions.why: Decides whether outstanding items are complete, how supplier open amounts are computed, and the call pattern.

questions.short: Where does the invoice header comment appear when the invoice is read back?
questions.why: Round-trip of reference and customer memo.

questions.short: Do date filters use calendar months or accounting periods, and do an API invoice’s period and VAT month always follow its date? Does the modified-after filter catch line and matching changes? Do accountant edits change entry ids or numbers, and are deletions signalled?
questions.why: Reliable incremental synchronisation and date filtering.

questions.short: What do several company fields mean (suspended activity, second name and address, family, contact person), how is an enterprise number written, which collective account applies by default, and does invoice creation check the partner’s customer or supplier flag?
questions.why: Mapping of active status, addresses, company numbers and receivable accounts, and partner checks on invoice creation.

questions.short: Can an account’s category be set, or is it derived from the number? What is the full list of categories, is it always filled for balance-sheet accounts, and does the account list include inactive and title accounts?
questions.why: Determines the Chift account type on creation and in the chart of accounts.

questions.short: How do analytics behave: what is returned for folders without the analytics module, which cost schemas must each line carry (rounding lines included), are there limits on cost lines, what do the schema flags mean, and is the cost-history balance signed?
questions.why: Analytics on write and the analytic routes on read.

questions.short: What does the daybook “used” flag mean, which daybook types accept API entries, does the fiscal-year list show whether a year is closed, and is a miscellaneous operation dated in a closed operations or VAT period refused, with which error?
questions.why: Journal flags and posting rules.

questions.short: Which related data can be included in the same call on the company, book-entry and account-history lists, and with which fields?
questions.why: Could reduce read-backs and invoice retrieval to fewer calls.

questions.short: Can fetching a single entry by id return an entry from another folder of the same licence? What does it return for a replaced or deleted entry, and does a replaced entry link to its successor?
questions.why: Read-backs and single-invoice reads.

questions.short: Can Chift get a test licence or test folder, can test data be removed (the API cannot delete companies or invoices), and are test licences hosted like production?
questions.why: The API works on live data, and the volume test must reflect production conditions.

questions.short: What is the maximum attachment size for uploads?
questions.why: Validation of PDFs sent with invoices.

questions.short: How does Chift register an integration (client credentials, redirect URIs, approval), and which Horus user should authorise the connection for an accounting firm and for an SMB so the right folders are visible?
questions.why: Registration is the first step, and the folders visible through the API depend on the authorising user’s access.

questions.short: Is docs.horus-software.be the authoritative API documentation, and is the apiary version linked in the case deprecated or for a different API version?
questions.why: Every mapping rests on the current documentation; the two versions were not compared.

questions.short: May every integration and user type confirm entries through the API, or can the accounting firm restrict it? What is blocked once confirmed, is confirmation the accountant’s final validation, and do unconfirmed entries count in balances, VAT returns and closings?
questions.why: Decides whether direct posting can be offered on every connection and what “draft” means for clients.

questions.short: How does Horus validate invoice amounts: does it refuse or recalculate VAT more than one cent off base × rate, how are header and line totals compared, is a zero-base line with VAT accepted, and which decimal precision applies?
questions.why: Defines how the connector books VAT and rounding.

questions.short: For outstanding items: which account types can be returned, do the summary totals cover exactly the returned lines, are unlinked or partly allocated payments returned, and does the confirmed-only filter also keep unconfirmed elements out of open amounts?
questions.why: Control totals, signs and completeness of the outstanding items route.

questions.short: Which web addresses can a licence's API address have (it comes back through the browser at activation), so the connector can check it before sending Chift's client secret? And how do connections behave over time: a second authorisation by the same user, a user who loses access to a folder, revocation by Chift, and token expiry?
questions.why: Safe activation (the client secret must never reach an unchecked address), token storage and offboarding for Chift's connections.

questions.short: On client creation: are contact fields returned on read, how are VAT and enterprise numbers stored, normalised and checked for duplicates (per folder or licence, also on update), and does one invalid IBAN fail the whole create?
questions.why: Round-trip of the client response, duplicate checks and error handling on client creation.

questions.short: Should each connection choose a posting mode, review (entries pushed unconfirmed for the accountant; proposed default) or direct (confirmed on push), possibly per folder? Is returning the status actually stored acceptable, and what does “draft” mean across Chift connectors?
questions.why: Confirmation in Horus means accountant validation, changes numbering and limits deletion; the API cannot delete invoices.

questions.short: Is a connector-built VAT-code list per folder (from the Horus tax-combination files) acceptable, with tax_code null on read when ambiguous? Should OSS codes cover only requested countries, and should consumer VAT amounts be booked exactly as sent (proposed)?
questions.why: Horus has no VAT-code list, accepts no VAT code on write, and its read-side VAT code is undocumented.

questions.short: For inputs Horus cannot store (for example withholding tax, accrual dates, line quantity, extra addresses, more than two decimals), should the connector reject or drop them? Which address wins when several are sent, and is connector-side logging enough without a warnings field?
questions.why: Consistent behaviour across Chift connectors.

questions.short: For values Horus does not hold, should reads return null or a default? Is the folder country worth one extra call per folder? Should create responses echo unstored request fields or match what a later read returns?
questions.why: Avoids misleading defaults and create responses that differ from later reads.

questions.short: Sign conventions: are refunds sent positive, discounts as negative lines, and negative invoice totals allowed? Without a readable document type, which misclassification is preferable? Should credit notes and unallocated payments be negative in outstanding items, and partial payments allocated oldest due date first?
questions.why: Input sign is unspecified, Horus hides document type on read, and invoice and outstanding views would sign credit notes differently.

questions.short: On a duplicate (VAT number, external reference, document number, or supplier, date and total for unnumbered bills), return an error or the existing record? Which error for a timed-out create with unknown outcome? How should force_merge combine client and supplier data?
questions.why: Duplicate and merge policy must match other connectors; Horus has no idempotency key and one identity per company.

questions.short: Is rejecting non-numeric numbers acceptable? For an invoice to be confirmed without a number: push as draft for review (proposed), reject, or generate the next number? May numbers be required, and is operation_number the entry number or a client reference?
questions.why: Horus does not number invoices itself and stores numbers as numbers; unnumbered entries cannot be found after accountant edits.

questions.short: What does partner_info.account_number mean, and is partner_info needed when Horus can create partners? Should a missing customer or supplier role be added or rejected, how should new third-party codes be generated, and how should same-name clients without identifiers be handled?
questions.why: account_number is undefined in the Chift spec, the code is visible to accountants, and unidentified clients cannot be reliably deduplicated.

questions.short: Is building analytic combinations from independent per-plan percentages acceptable? Should Free-type Horus dimensions be hidden from analytic plans (proposed)? Are slightly different read-back distributions on small amounts acceptable, and should plans covering only part of a line be omitted?
questions.why: Horus allocates amounts to combinations of cost sections.

questions.short: Should unconfirmed entries be returned as drafts or excluded by default? Is an invoice id changing after an accountant edit acceptable? Do consumers rely on updated_after for status changes like “paid”, and what periodic full re-sync is acceptable?
questions.why: In review mode every pushed invoice stays unconfirmed until the accountant confirms it; excluding them by default would hide them.

questions.short: What default period should invoice retrieval use without dates (proposed: current fiscal year), how far back must updated_after polls look, and are consumers expected to dedupe items re-sent by a safety overlap?
questions.why: Horus needs a month window and cannot page lists; the default and look-back drive the cost of every read.

questions.short: Should the Horus connector always enable multiple folders? Does the platform block folder ids not selected at activation, or must the connector? Can several Chift consumers share one Horus licence, and who activates the connector for a firm-managed SMB?
questions.why: Accounting-firm licences hold many folders, and one Horus token sees every folder its user can access.

questions.short: Can a connector cache reference data per folder, and results between page calls of one request? What is the synchronous request timeout, and is there a background pattern for heavy reads?
questions.why: Horus lists cannot be paged; without a cache every page call re-reads the whole period.

questions.short: For foreign-currency miscellaneous operations, does Chift core convert amounts to EUR before calling the connector, or must the connector? Which rate direction applies, how is a rounding residue absorbed, and should the response show the original currency or EUR?
questions.why: Horus operation lines have no currency field, and Chift requires a rate for operations in another currency.

questions.short: Horus gives an explicit invoice-currency amount only for open sales invoices; ledger lines carry a currency code and rate whose meaning H4 must confirm. Should open sales invoices keep their currency (they switch to euro once paid), or should foreign-currency invoices always come back in EUR at rate 1 (favoured)? Which rate direction, and are mixed-currency outstanding items acceptable?
questions.why: Consumers syncing with updated_after would see an invoice change currency; Chift does not define the rate direction.

questions.short: For outstanding items: one item per invoice with several due dates, or one per due-date line (proposed)? Should unallocated payments and credit balances appear? Are per-partner matching numbers acceptable as they are, and should employee items be excluded?
questions.why: Chift lists all due dates per item while Horus has one per ledger line; this changes open items and totals.

questions.short: When a list filter cannot be applied exactly on Horus (approval status, unknown journal id, estimated account types), return 400, ignore it, or return a best-effort result? Is Horus “Verified” an acceptable stand-in for “approved”?
questions.why: Silent empty or approximate results are hard for consumers to detect; behaviour should match other connectors.

questions.short: On invoice creation, how large a header/line difference may invoice_correction absorb before rejection, and should lines whose tax departs from untaxed amount × rate beyond a tolerance be rejected?
questions.why: Without limits, real data errors would be booked on the correction account or as VAT.

questions.short: Which status and error_code do other connectors use for validation errors without a predefined code, re-authorisation, persistent upstream errors and unknown create outcomes? Should VAT numbers with dots or spaces be rejected or normalised, and does the platform retry after timeouts?
questions.why: Consumers branch on status and error_code, which must match other connectors.
